newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton called to open 0.10 cent firmer.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton called to open 0.10 cent firmer.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures were called to open 0.10 cent firmer Friday, based on market orders at 1019 EDT, trading sources said.
Thursday, speculative shortcovering buoyed prices during the day, but trade selling capped gains and knocked the market off the highs by the close.
The new-crop December contract settled 0.23 cent higher at 75.63 cents a lb. Spot July ended up 0.09 cent at 72.62 cents, while the rest of the board finished 0.25 to 0.10 cent higher.
Resistance in December delivery was pegged at 75.60 cents, followed by 76.10 cents. Support was seen at 75.10 cents.

Traders await the expiry of the spot July contract on June 24. Analysts expect the market to focus on spread activity aheadof expiry, and then turn its attention to the fundamentals and the new crop development.
While cotton in the Delta and the Southeast is behind schedule, warmer temperatures forecast for the next several days is expected to help the development of the crop.
California and Arizona cotton is in good condition.
